item.title: Brazilians vote in presidential election runoff pitting leftist Lula against far-right Bolsonaro
item.description:
Incumbent president lost in first round to senator and son of convicted ex-president

Brazilians are going to the polls on Sunday in a highly unpredictable runoff in which the leftist president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is attempting an unprecedented comeback against the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who won the first-round vote.

Bolsonaro’s surprise victory despite not leading most polls made him the favourite three weeks ago, but since then Lula’s campaign has gained ground, and the two go into the contest virtually tied.

item.title: Ten days that could shake the world: democratic norms at stake in four pivotal elections
item.description:
Brazil, Israel, Serbia and the US are holding elections within the space of 10 days. Will the authoritarian right cement its global gains, or can pro-democracy forces make a comeback?

Four elections on four continents within 10 days could profoundly reshape global politics, propelling the world further along its current authoritarian trajectory or marking a limited comeback for democratic norms.

In all four contests, basic democratic norms are at stake at a time when autocracy is advancing worldwide at an alarming rate. According to the Sweden-based V-Dem Institute, which uses multivariable assessment tools, the democratic freedoms enjoyed by the average global citizen are down to levels last seen in 1978 – long before the fall of the Berlin Wall and the collapse of communism in Europe.

More than one million supporters of Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, have streamed on to Rio’s most famous beach for a giant protest they hope will propel him towards a historic election fightback against his far-right rival, Flávio Bolsonaro.

Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election’s runoff on Sunday, with the pair tied in the polls after Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October by 47% to 45%.

item.title: ‘Bolso shows all signs of fascism’: the journalist who predicted Brazil’s future – and paid the ultimate price
item.description:
Dom Phillips warned that Jair Bolsonaro would make life more dangerous for reporters and the Amazon rainforest, and that his sons were even more extreme

“Bolso shows all signs of fascism, as do his supporters,” the murdered British journalist Dom Phillips told me before his death. “His sons are all more extreme if anything.”

These words were written in 2018 by the Guardian contributor shortly before the election of the far-right former army captain Jair Bolsonaro as president of Brazil – a prospect that Dom viewed with dread.

Organized Crime Postponed Democracy in Haiti, Again

As criminal governance becomes entrenched, the question about Haiti’s return to democracy is not when but how. 

In a briefing on October 19, the United Nations’ top delegate to Haiti, Carlos Ruiz Massieu told the UN Security Council that the country is still far from holding its first national elections since 2016.

item.title: Haiti in Crisis: Why Elections Are Impossible Right Now | The InSight Take
item.description:
Haiti in Crisis: Why Elections Are Impossible Right Now | The InSight Take

Haiti elections are currently non-existent, leaving a power vacuum that empowers criminal groups. Steven Dudley sits down with investigator Alex Papadovasilakis to analyze the dire political and security landscape in Port-au-Prince. With the absence of elected leadership, the state has struggled to maintain authority, allowing gang control to expand significantly across the nation. We break down how the erosion of democratic institutions has facilitated this shift and what it means for regional stability.

The post Haiti in Crisis: Why Elections Are Impossible Right Now | The InSight Take appeared first on InSight Crime.

item.title: Jorge Luis Zambrano, alias “Rasquiña”
item.description:
Jorge Luis Zambrano, alias “Rasquiña”

Jorge Luis Zambrano, alias “Rasquiña” or “JL,” was the charismatic leader of the Choneros, which, for years, was Ecuador’s most enterprising and powerful criminal group. Rasquiña oversaw the group’s transformation from a localized criminal group into a nationwide prison-based criminal federation with links to transnational drug-trafficking organizations. He was assassinated in 2020.

The post Jorge Luis Zambrano, alias “Rasquiña” appeared first on InSight Crime.
